subject: ARA
label: Grade 09
task: Meet the outcome of every unit in Grade 09 Arabic, and keep one piece of evidence for each.
condition: A 36-week school year, 4 units, a teacher or guide, a learning book or device, and local examples in the local language first with English support.
standard: Each unit: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer. Course pass: no unit at 'Not yet' after one retry, and a pass in SA1 and SA2.

modules.title: Seasons and comparison
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Seasons and comparison', taught in a way that is with notes, a worked line and a self-mark. The target is clear: compare two seasons in writing. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Seasons and comparison' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: compare two seasons in writing, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: الصيف أحرّ من الشتاء. الشتاء أبرد من الصيف. (Summer is hotter than winter. Winter is colder than summer.) Method: Model run for 'Seasons and comparison'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 30 to 40 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: a worked task and a corrected copy.
modules.standard: Compare two seasons in writing: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer.
steps: Step 1, Plan a comparison. Choose two seasons, here summer and winter, and list points to compare: temperature, rain, activities, feeling. Then write a topic sentence: الصَّيْفُ وَالشِّتَاءُ فَصْلَانِ مُخْتَلِفَانِ. [Summer and winter are two different seasons.]

Step 2, Use the comparative adjective أَفْعَلُ مِنْ. الصَّيْفُ أَكْثَرُ حَرَارَةً مِنَ الشِّتَاءِ. [Summer is hotter than winter.] الشِّتَاءُ أَبْرَدُ وَأَكْثَرُ مَطَرًا. [Winter is colder and rainier.] The word مِنْ introduces the thing compared.

Step 3, Contrast with linking words. بَيْنَمَا الشِّتَاءُ بَارِدٌ، فَإِنَّ الصَّيْفَ حَارٌّ. [While winter is cold, summer is hot.] فِي الصَّيْفِ نَسْبَحُ فِي الْبَحْرِ، أَمَّا فِي الشِّتَاءِ فَنَجْلِسُ قُرْبَ الْمِدْفَأَةِ. [In summer we swim in the sea, whereas in winter we sit by the heater.]

Step 4, Conclude with your preference. أُفَضِّلُ الشِّتَاءَ لِأَنَّ الْجَوَّ هَادِئٌ وَأُحِبُّ صَوْتَ الْمَطَرِ. [I prefer winter because the weather is calm and I love the sound of rain.] Read all four sentences together and check each has a clear link.

Step 5, Fix an error. A student writes الصَّيْفُ أَكْثَرُ حَرَارَةً الشِّتَاءِ. Correction: add مِنَ: الصَّيْفُ أَكْثَرُ حَرَارَةً مِنَ الشِّتَاءِ. Another says الصَّيْفُ حَارٌّ وَالشِّتَاءُ بَارِدٌ only; that lists, not compares. Use أَكْثَرُ and مِنْ.

Step 6, Your turn: write three sentences comparing spring and autumn. Model answer: الرَّبِيعُ أَجْمَلُ مِنَ الْخَرِيفِ لِأَنَّ الْأَزْهَارَ تَتَفَتَّحُ. بَيْنَمَا يَكُونُ الْخَرِيفُ أَهْدَأَ. أُفَضِّلُ الرَّبِيعَ. [Spring is more beautiful than autumn because flowers open. While autumn is calmer. I prefer spring.]

modules.title: Neighbours and community
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Neighbours and community', taught in a way that is with notes, a worked line and a self-mark. The target is clear: describe community life. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Neighbours and community' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: describe community life, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: للجار حق على جاره. أساعد جارتي وأسلّم عليها. (A neighbour has a right over a neighbour. I help my neighbour and greet her.) Method: Model run for 'Neighbours and community'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 30 to 40 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: a worked task and a corrected copy.
modules.standard: Describe community life: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer.
steps: Step 1, Name community words. الْجَارُ [neighbour], الْحَيُّ [neighbourhood], التَّعَاوُنُ [cooperation], الْمُسَاعَدَةُ [help], الْمَرِيضُ [the sick person], الْمُسِنُّ [the elderly]. Use them in a mind map around the word الْمُجْتَمَعُ [society].

Step 2, Describe your neighbourhood. يَسْكُنُ بِجَوَارِنَا جَارٌ طَيِّبٌ. [A kind neighbour lives next to us.] يَتَعَاوَنُ أَهْلُ الْحَيِّ فِي تَنْظِيفِ الشَّارِعِ. [The people of the neighbourhood cooperate in cleaning the street.] نَزُورُ الْمَرِيضَ وَنُسَاعِدُ الْمُسِنَّ. [We visit the sick and help the elderly.]

Step 3, Use relative clauses. الْجَارُ الَّذِي يُسَاعِدُنَا طَيِّبٌ. [The neighbour who helps us is kind.] The relative pronoun الَّذِي is used after a definite noun. After an indefinite noun leave it out: جَارٌ يُسَاعِدُنَا [a neighbour who helps us].

Step 4, Write a paragraph. الْحَيُّ الَّذِي أَسْكُنُ فِيهِ هَادِئٌ. يَجْتَمِعُ الْجِيرَانُ فِي الْأَعْيَادِ وَيَتَبَادَلُونَ الْحَلْوَى. لِذَلِكَ نَشْعُرُ بِالْأَمَانِ وَالْمَحَبَّةِ. [The neighbourhood I live in is quiet. Neighbours gather at festivals and exchange sweets. So we feel safe and loved.]

Step 5, Fix an error. A student writes جَارٌ الَّذِي يُسَاعِدُنَا. Correction: جَارٌ يُسَاعِدُنَا without الَّذِي, because جَارٌ is indefinite; or الْجَارُ الَّذِي يُسَاعِدُنَا with a definite noun. Also match the pronoun: الَّتِي for a feminine noun.

Step 6, Your turn: write a short paragraph about how your neighbourhood helps people. Model answer: فِي حَيِّنَا جِيرَانٌ يَتَعَاوَنُونَ. الْمَرْأَةُ الَّتِي تَسْكُنُ بِجَانِبِنَا تُسَاعِدُ الْمُسِنِّينَ. هَكَذَا يَكُونُ الْمُجْتَمَعُ قَوِيًّا. [In our neighbourhood neighbours cooperate. The woman who lives next to us helps the elderly. This is how society becomes strong.]

modules.title: Grammar: sentence types
modules.outcome: use nominal and verbal sentences correctly
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Grammar: sentence types', taught in a way that is with notes, a worked line and a self-mark. The target is clear: use nominal and verbal sentences correctly. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Grammar: sentence types' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: use nominal and verbal sentences correctly, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: جملة اسمية: الطالب مجتهد. جملة فعلية: ذهب الطالب إلى المدرسة. Method: Model run for 'Grammar: sentence types'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 30 to 40 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: a worked task and a corrected copy.
modules.standard: Use nominal and verbal sentences correctly: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer.
steps: Step 1, A nominal sentence (جُمْلَةٌ اسْمِيَّةٌ) begins with a noun: الْوَلَدُ مُجْتَهِدٌ. [The boy is hardworking.] It has a subject (مُبْتَدَأٌ) الْوَلَدُ and a predicate (خَبَرٌ) مُجْتَهِدٌ, both in the nominative.

Step 2, A verbal sentence (جُمْلَةٌ فِعْلِيَّةٌ) begins with a verb: يَكْتُبُ الطَّالِبُ الدَّرْسَ. [The student writes the lesson.] Parts: verb يَكْتُبُ, doer (فَاعِلٌ) الطَّالِبُ in the nominative, object (مَفْعُولٌ بِهِ) الدَّرْسَ in the accusative.

Step 3, Compare the order. الطَّالِبُ يَكْتُبُ الدَّرْسَ is a nominal sentence, because it begins with a noun; its predicate is the verbal phrase يَكْتُبُ الدَّرْسَ. Both mean the same, but the grammar name depends on the first word.

Step 4, After إِنَّ the subject becomes accusative. إِنَّ الطَّالِبَ مُجْتَهِدٌ. [Indeed the student is hardworking.] Contrast with the plain sentence الطَّالِبُ مُجْتَهِدٌ. Now analyse: كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ رِسَالَةً. [The boy wrote a letter.] Verb كَتَبَ, doer الْوَلَدُ, object رِسَالَةً.

Step 5, Fix an error. A student calls الطَّالِبُ يَكْتُبُ a verbal sentence. Correction: it begins with a noun, so it is nominal. Another writes كَتَبَ الْوَلَدَ رِسَالَةً with a fatha on الْوَلَدَ; the doer takes damma: كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ رِسَالَةً.

Step 6, Your turn: analyse يَقْرَأُ الْوَلَدُ الْكِتَابَ and write one nominal sentence. Model answer: verbal; verb يَقْرَأُ, doer الْوَلَدُ, object الْكِتَابَ. Nominal: الْكِتَابُ مُفِيدٌ. [The book is useful.] Subject and predicate are both nominative.

modules.title: Essay writing
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Essay writing', taught in a way that is with notes, a worked line and a self-mark. The target is clear: write a short essay. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Essay writing' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: write a short essay, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: فقرة: القراءة مفيدة. فهي تزيد معلوماتنا. وتنمّي لغتنا. لذلك أقرأ كل يوم. (topic sentence, two details, closing) Method: Model run for 'Essay writing'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 30 to 40 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: a worked task and a corrected copy.
modules.standard: Write a short essay: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer.
steps: Step 1, An essay has three parts: introduction (مُقَدِّمَةٌ), body (عَرْضٌ), conclusion (خَاتِمَةٌ). Topic: the importance of reading. Open with a general claim: الْقِرَاءَةُ غِذَاءُ الْعَقْلِ، وَهِيَ مِفْتَاحُ الْمَعْرِفَةِ. [Reading is food for the mind and the key to knowledge.]

Step 2, Write the first body paragraph. أَوَّلًا، تُوَسِّعُ الْقِرَاءَةُ مَعْلُومَاتِنَا. فَالْكِتَابُ يَأْخُذُنَا إِلَى بِلَادٍ لَمْ نَزُرْهَا. [First, reading widens our knowledge. A book takes us to countries we have not visited.] Give a claim, then an explanation.

Step 3, Write the second paragraph. ثَانِيًا، تُحَسِّنُ الْقِرَاءَةُ لُغَتَنَا وَتُنَمِّي خَيَالَنَا. فَمَنْ يَقْرَأُ كَثِيرًا يَكْتُبُ بِأُسْلُوبٍ أَجْمَلَ. [Second, reading improves our language and develops our imagination. Whoever reads a lot writes in a nicer style.]

Step 4, Conclude. لِذَلِكَ عَلَيْنَا أَنْ نَجْعَلَ الْقِرَاءَةَ عَادَةً يَوْمِيَّةً. [Therefore we must make reading a daily habit.] A conclusion restates the claim in different words and ends with advice. Never introduce a new argument here.

Step 5, Fix an error. A student writes one block with no introduction and repeats the same point three times. Correction: divide into introduction, two body paragraphs with different arguments, and a conclusion, and link them with أَوَّلًا، ثَانِيًا، لِذَلِكَ.

Step 6, Your turn: outline and write an introduction for the essay The value of time. Model answer: الْوَقْتُ أَثْمَنُ مَا نَمْلِكُ، وَمَنْ أَحْسَنَ اسْتِعْمَالَهُ نَجَحَ. [Time is the most precious thing we own, and whoever uses it well succeeds.] Outline: 1 planning, 2 avoiding waste, 3 result.

ladder: L1: say and read familiar words and short sentences.
L2: read short texts and write connected sentences.
L3: write paragraphs and speak on a topic with notes.
L4: write for different purposes and analyse how texts persuade.
L5: write and argue at length; handle unseen texts.
L6 (degree): academic reading, writing and citation.
L7 (postgraduate): publish, teach or translate with expert accuracy.
